A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Prune2Drive. All 13 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Their methods, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material support reliable comparison despite reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original DriveLM and DriveLMM-o1 evaluations, inference-efficiency measurements, ablations, and qualitative token-selection results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds general VLM benchmark results, video-driving evaluation, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and failure cases.

M1.justification: T-FPS, Algorithm 1, and the view-specific ratio-search procedure retain their operational components. Section 3.2 reformulates the optimization using a frozen model and retention ratios, but does not establish an implemented procedure change. The additional benchmarks likewise introduce no documented pruning component or temporal adaptation.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained DriveLM and DriveLMM-o1 coverage, v2 evaluates GQA, VQA V2, POPE, VizWiz, and MME, plus multi-frame driving on OmniDrive. This substantially broadens coverage to general visual understanding, hallucination assessment, images from blind users, and temporal driving inputs.

E2.justification: FastV, DART, SparseVLM, and PACT remain in the corresponding driving comparisons; FastV and SparseVLM remain the efficiency comparators. The added benchmarks reuse existing comparators. DART's change from a dated label to EMNLP25 identifies the same method.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce LLaVA-1.5-7B with 576-token reference inputs and 128/64-token retention, plus DriveMM on OmniDrive at 10% retention using BLEU, CIDEr, ROUGE, and an average score. The original driving evaluation settings, 75%/90% pruning conditions, and A100 efficiency protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Existing distance-metric and search-strategy ablations and qualitative comparisons are retained. Supplementary Sections C.2 and D.3 add two targeted analyses: failure cases involving sparsely retained safety-critical vehicles, and a three-point sensitivity sweep over lambda values 0.04, 0.05, and 0.06.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. The new lambda sweep measures parameter sensitivity, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: The matched original benchmark, efficiency, and ablation tables retain their numerical values. v2 substantially expands results through Tables 3 and 5, reporting general-VLM performance and an OmniDrive average of 49.0 versus 50.3 for the unpruned model. It also adds sensitivity scores of 58.2/58.3/58.1 and T-FPS overhead measurements, and revises reported optimization time from 10 to 3 H100 GPU hours.

T1.justification: New Section 3.3 introduces a view-weighted Lipschitz assumption, a Hausdorff-distance definition, and a theorem claiming a tighter error bound than uniform-ratio random sampling, accompanied by an informal argument. Section 3.2 also replaces the earlier bilevel-style expression with direct frozen-model optimization and explicitly defines the penalty over retained tokens.

C1.justification: The two central contributions and headline driving-efficiency claims remain unchanged. The revised conclusion additionally claims effectiveness and scalability on conventional VLM benchmarks and video-driving tasks, modestly broadening the stated applicability beyond the original emphasis.

C2.justification: The applicability discussion changes substantially: v1's single-frame-only limitation and proposed video extension are replaced by a limitation concerning absent closed-loop evaluation and uncertain interactive behavior. v2 also identifies a concrete safety-relevant failure mechanism: visually homogeneous objects can receive too few tokens. The new video results are interpreted as evidence of spatial-temporal feature preservation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository address, reports T-FPS overhead of 0.02 seconds for 729 tokens and less than 0.1% of total FLOPs, and adds benchmark descriptions. Reported optimization time changes from 10 to 3 H100 GPU hours, while the disclosed 500-sample search and 100-iteration limit remain unchanged. These disclosures do not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 adds contextual citations including MJ-Bench, Kimi K2.5, and Mixing Importance with Diversity. The related-work argument and positioning against attention-based and single-image pruning remain largely unchanged. Consolidated duplicate references and DART's venue update do not represent new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract, rewrites Section 3.2, lightly edits surrounding prose, and introduces a separate supplementary heading with more explicit subsection numbering. Most existing paragraphs and the overall narrative order are retained; the revision is not an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3, 5, and 9 and failure-case Figure 6, redraws the Figure 2 radar display, and changes caption placement and table sizing, including a single-column efficiency table. Figures 1, 4, and 5 reuse identical image content, and the architecture diagram is retained. The remaining differences mainly concern formatting and reflow.

improvement.justification: Broader general-VLM and temporal-driving tests strengthen the empirical evidence, while concrete failure cases, clearer deployment limitations, and a documented code link improve transparency. These gains are tempered by weaknesses: Section 3.3 does not sufficiently derive its claimed dominance guarantee, and the new VLM discussion reports a 7.5% gap where Table 3 shows 94.6% versus 86.9%. The retained original evidence and useful additions support a limited overall improvement, rather than a major gain in rigor.
